recipient: Mr. & Mrs. M.F. Weckel, 645 N. Broadview, Wichita, Kansas 67208, U.S.A.
notes: Front: night view of the Hongkong Hilton tower, lit windows against the dark hillside and dense high-rise skyline of Hong Kong Island. Back copy: 'The Far East's most dramatic hotel; on Hong Kong Island, overlooking [the] harbor, in the Colony's central area. Fine restaurants and bars, two night clubs, 80-Ft. swimming pool and Island Cruising Brigantine.' HK$1 Queen Elizabeth II definitive stamp; postmark Hong Kong, 23 Jul 1979, sent airmail. Message: 'Dear Gladys & Maurice, We have finally arrived in Hong Kong and find it everything we had hoped for. The trip over was mixed. Hawaii fine, Japan awful and so on. We start looking for a place to live tomorrow. Hope that work[s] out. Love from all, Dolores.' Addressed to Mr. & Mrs. M.F. Weckel, 645 N. Broadview, Wichita, Kansas — this card gives the fullest form of the recipients' names yet seen in the archive, 'Gladys & Maurice,' confirming 'M.F. Weckel' as Maurice F. Weckel; it also matches the 'Aunt Gladys & Uncle Babe' salutation on the Dana Point card in this same batch (id 231), suggesting 'Babe' was Maurice's nickname. The Weckels of 645 N. Broadview, Wichita, now recur across at least seven cards in the archive (ids 200, 213, 215, 216, 230, 231, and this one), a well-documented correspondence circle receiving travel postcards from many different family members and friends over roughly two decades.

location: Evanston, Wyoming (postmark) — a Western tall-tale jackalope scene
recipient: Elmer & Tillie Geis, 205 So. Freeborn, Marion, Kansas 66861
notes: Front: a tall-tale postcard, 'Saddling Up Big Jack' — a cowboy saddling an enormous jackrabbit as though it were a horse, real horses tethered along a white rail fence behind him. Back caption: 'It is not unusual to break these big fellows and use them for ranch work.' Distributed by Geo Mc. Co., Salt Lake City, Utah, as 'The Continental Card'; © Mike Roberts Color Productions, Emeryville, Calif. (code B8317). 10-cent 'People's Right to Petition for Redress' stamp (part of the 1976 Bicentennial Bill of Rights series); postmark Evanston, Wyo., Aug 16 (year not fully legible on this scan, but consistent with 1976 given the stamp). Message, headed 'Aug 17, Sun. evening, 8PM': 'Dear Onee — We drove all day thru Wyoming. We are at Evanston, Wyo. tonight, will be on the line tomorrow; will head to Salt Lake City and then on. We found Rene & family fine at Arvada. Martha & Mal were good, we were surprised how well he looked. Lapole & I stayed at their place, Gus & Lou at a motel. Really fell in love with Loveland. We also visited Geo. Harmon, Lapole's friend, at Loveland. We drove in rain after we left at 3:30 AM from Marion on to Harper. Things were nice & green in western Ks. We are having a nice time, sure get tired. Don't believe everything you see on the front of this card — we haven't seen any rabbits yet, but antelope & deer. We miss you all. See you in a couple weeks. Love, Lapole & Bea.' A postscript adds: '53° at Loveland this morning, 78 today. Really soaking it in, wearing sweaters.' Addressed to Elmer & Tillie Geis, 205 So. Freeborn, Marion, Kansas — the itinerary (Marion, Ks. to Harper to western Kansas to Arvada, Colo. to Loveland, Colo. to Evanston, Wyo., headed toward Salt Lake City) traces a loop through Kansas, Colorado, and Wyoming.
